plan: Given my value of $10, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit while minimizing risk. Assuming others bid near their values, I will bid $9.9. This bid allows me to win if others undervalue or bid conservatively, while limiting losses if outbid. Bidding higher risks negative profit if I win and pay close to my value. With no history, I assume a balanced approach from others, neither too aggressive nor too conservative. This bid maximizes expected profit by balancing potential win probability and cost.

Given my value of $30, I aim to maximize profit by bidding slightly below my value to potentially win without overpaying. Assuming opponents bid near their values, a bid of $25 could outbid a cautious opponent and still yield profit if I win. By bidding $25, I win if others bid below $25, gaining a net profit of $30 minus the second-highest bid. This balances winning chances with profit maximization.

Given my private value of $25, I should bid below my value to ensure a profit if I win. Assuming others bid near their values, I aim to bid slightly lower than $25 to outbid them while securing a profit. I'll bid $24.9 to balance winning potential with profit. This strategy maximizes my chances of winning while ensuring a profit margin if the second-highest bid is slightly lower than my bid.
